session.assigned: match emission width to the measured localization error
session.over_budget_reason: two wrong starts before the right harness: the greedy exact-U sweep was intractable at this arm count and the budget-filling sweep was written with a per-segment full-grid boolean AND, which made it quadratic.

question: Does emitting parallel dotted lines at the measured across-strike sigma beat a single tight line, at an equal dot budget, under the exact GEMS metric?
answer: Yes on the holdout, no in the idealised model, and the disagreement is explained. At an identical 44,090-dot budget per fold, five lines at 0/+/-3/+/-6 px score 0.059635 HOLDOUT-DTI against 0.044854 for the tight line, a relative gain of 33.0 %. The analytic model predicted the opposite because it assumed an infinitely long fault, where the along-strike dot stride can be raised without limit to pay for the extra lines; real ridge segments are short, so it cannot.

datasets.features: organizer geodawn numerical stack, 19 usable bands, 3730x3292 at 100 m
datasets.ridge_field: gems58w.extract cached ridge field v2 (hessian, 3 scales, non-max suppressed)
datasets.inventory: registry/registry_merged.json, 703 pinned public sibling rasters, 694 restored and sha256-verified this session, 9 unrestorable

experiments.name: sigma table
experiments.what: measured the across-strike and along-strike distance from every withheld catalogue component to the nearest candidate ridge, split by data block, feature resolution and ridge type, cross-fitted leave-one-block-out
experiments.finding: pooled median across-strike sigma 4.30 px (p25 2.38, p75 7.01, 1,425 matched components); sigma falls slowly as feature resolution coarsens (5.09 px at 1.5 px to 4.09 px at 6 px) and gravity crests localise worst (6.06 px). Because every block sits within +-1 px of the pooled median, block-to-block variation carries almost no information.

experiments.name: equal-budget geometry sweep
experiments.what: seven ribbon geometries, each fitted to the SAME 44,090-dot budget per fold and the same ridge segments, scored with the exact metric
experiments.note: the per-segment sigma-adaptive width (ADAPT) ranks LAST, so the sigma stratification measured in EXP-1 does not transfer to individual segments: it describes classes, not instances.

experiments.name: emission, validation and uniqueness screen
experiments.what: emitted the winning geometry on the catalogue-free domain, scored the delivered bytes on all four folds against an empty control, validated the file, and screened it against all 694 restored public rasters
experiments.finding: delivered-bytes HOLDOUT-DTI 0.038249 (95 % CI 0.032263-0.043873), 43867 dots, 0 on the catalogue, median distance to it 20.6 px

leakage_canary.verdict: PASS: no feature alone separates withheld truth above the limit. The worst is 0.8950, close enough to the 0.90 tripwire that it should be re-run if the feature set changes.

gates.name: Uniqueness — literal >70% reading (hard stop under the current brief)

stop_conditions_hit: literal uniqueness rule: 81 of 694 witnesses show > 70 % of my dots within 3 px of theirs, which under the standing instruction means log the duplicate and stop.

second_reading.note: open owner decision, never closed by a script

proven: ribbon width beats a tight line at an equal dot budget on catalogue holdout
the delivered file is unique in bytes and in pixels among all 694 checked rasters
no single feature leaks withheld truth above the 0.90 AUC tripwire
not_proven: that the holdout gain transfers to the organizer's private new-fault truth
that any of this beats the public leaderboard: no organizer receipt exists, so no ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED score can be quoted
that the artifact is not a duplicate under the literal rule
dead_ends: lazy CELF greedy over (segment, offset) arms: intractable at ~3.5k arms
per-segment full-grid boolean AND in the budget fill: quadratic, ~10 min/fold
equal-dot-density simulation as the decision rule: it is a stride artifact
per-segment sigma as a width selector: loses to a fixed 5-line ribbon
